We want [quarto.org](https://quarto.org) to work for everyone.
As one part of that commitment, this page shows the results of the [latest automated accessibility scan](#latest-scan) of the site.

## How the scan works

Every week, we run [`quarto call axe`](https://{{< prerelease-docs-url 1.11 >}}quarto.org/docs/websites/website-accessibility.html), which checks every page with [axe-core](https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core). Each page is checked at a desktop and a phone viewport, and in light and dark mode.

Findings we know about and cannot fix in this site are recorded in [`_axe-baseline.json`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/blob/main/_axe-baseline.json). Each entry says why it is accepted, who owns the fix, and when it can be removed. Most are defects in third-party libraries that the documentation demonstrates, or defects in Quarto itself that a linked quarto-cli issue tracks.

Pull requests to quarto.org run a smaller scan of the pages they change. The check fails if a pull request adds a new serious or critical finding.

## Reporting a problem

If you find an accessibility problem on [quarto.org](https://quarto.org), please [open an issue](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/new).
